analysis:
Reviewed SandboxInstaller.swift and SandboxSetupCommand.swift, which add a repeatable `--disk` work-disk option to `darkbloom sandbox setup`. Relevant boundary: TB-013/T-061 (CLI downloads and runs the add-on installer as the Mac owner, A-019). Nothing in the diff weakens the existing HTTPS-only download, redirect restriction, size cap, or owner-only staging.

Disk paths reach the installer as separate argv elements to /bin/sh through SandboxChildProcess.run (SandboxInstaller.swift:137, SandboxSetupCommand.swift plan and install calls). There is no shell interpolation, so I found no command injection. The `--disk` flag is only passed to installers whose text names it (`supportsDisks`). That check is a substring match on a script the service controls, but that script already runs as the owner under the existing T-061 trust, so this adds no new privilege.

New local-privilege behavior: `checkWorkDisks` / `turnOnOwnership` can run `sudo diskutil enableOwnership <mount>` through the `enableOwnership` hook. It only runs on an interactive terminal, without `--yes`, after an explicit confirm, and only when the sole problem is ownership off. The mount point comes from the `SandboxWorkDisk.volume` lookup, which was not supplied.

Minor observations, not findings:
- In the fresh path, `checkMac` runs `checkWorkDisks` (and may offer to turn ownership on) before the installer download confirms `--disk` support. A later 'Nothing changed' message could then be inaccurate.
- Installer stderr lines are echoed to the terminal on plan failure (the last 5 lines), a pre-existing pattern.

Not verifiable from the supplied evidence: SandboxWorkDisk (absolutePath, volume, check, problem, candidates, enableOwnership) and the add-on's installer-side validation of disks. Open questions for integration: whether absolutePath rejects or neutralizes values starting with '-', and whether external work disks must be encrypted. VM images and job data on an operator-chosen external drive sit outside the attested boundary, similar to the T-041 cache-storage caveats, and the CLI only checks for APFS with ownership on. The threat model may need a TB-013 note covering this.
